Maximal Fat Oxidation Kinetics (SIN Model)

Source: R/MFO_kinetics.R
MFO_kinetics.Rd

Fit the SIN model (Cheneviere et al., 2009) to describe fat oxidation kinetics and extract three parameters: dilatation (d), symmetry (s), and translation (t). Also calculates Fatmin (the intensity where fat oxidation reaches zero), which is a unique capability of the SIN model over polynomial methods.

Usage

MFO_kinetics(MFO_data, fatmin_threshold = NULL)

Arguments

MFO_data

a data frame obtained from the MFO function (must contain FAT and porc_VO2 columns).

fatmin_threshold

`NULL` (default) for Fatmin at the second zero of the curve, or a proportion of MFO in (0, 1), e.g. 0.05, for the intensity above Fatmax where fat oxidation falls to that fraction of MFO (closed form: \[(pi + 2d) ((pi - asin(threshold)) / pi)^(1/s) - d - t\] / K). v0.2.0 used a fixed 5 % threshold searched on a grid.

Value

Returns a list which contains:

  • MFO_kinetics_data: `MFO_data` plus normalized %MFO (`porc_MFO`, 100 = highest observed FAT).

  • MFO_kinetics_plot: ggplot object with the observed %MFO, the basic SIN and the fitted SIN.

  • d: dilatation parameter (width of the curve).

  • t: translation parameter (horizontal shift along intensity axis).

  • s: symmetry parameter (controls curve shape asymmetry; <1 left-skew, >1 right-skew).

  • Fatmin: exercise intensity (% VO2max) at the second zero of the curve, or at `fatmin_threshold` of MFO if given.

  • FatMax_SIN: exercise intensity (% VO2max) at peak fat oxidation from SIN model.

  • R_squared: R-squared of the SIN model fit (observed proportions of MFO).

  • RMSE: Root mean squared error of the SIN model fit (proportion of MFO).

  • d_se: standard error of dilatation parameter.

  • s_se: standard error of symmetry parameter.

  • t_se: standard error of translation parameter.

  • convergence: logical, whether the SIN model converged.

Details

The model is equation \[14\] of Cheneviere et al. (2009, Med Sci Sports Exerc 41: 1615-1625, p. 1618, doi:10.1249/MSS.0b013e31819e2f91 ): $$\%MFO = \sin\{[\pi^{1/s} / (\pi + 2d) \cdot (Kx + d + t)]^s\}, \quad K = \pi/100,$$ x in % VO2max. Up to v0.2.0 the package computed (pi^(1/s)/pi) + 2d, so its `d` (and `t`) are not comparable with published values (SPEC 6.5, 19).

Fitting procedure

As in Cheneviere et al. (2009), the model is fitted by non-linear least squares (Levenberg-Marquardt, [minpack.lm::nlsLM()], start d = 0, s = 1, t = 0) directly to the observed rows of `MFO_data`, with fat oxidation expressed as a proportion of the highest observed value (%MFO / 100). There is no smoothing and no synthetic grid: v0.1.0/v0.2.0 fitted the SIN to a fine grid predicted by a third-degree polynomial, which inflated n and shrank the standard errors of d, s and t (SPEC 19, finding 7). R-squared and RMSE are computed on the observed proportions. At least 4 rows are needed for 3 parameters: with fewer the function warns and returns `convergence = FALSE`; with 4 or 5 it fits but warns that the fit is unreliable and that at least 6 steps are recommended (SPEC 6.5).

`FatMax_SIN` and `Fatmin` come from closed forms derived from eq. \[14\]: Fatmax = \[(pi + 2d) 2^(-1/s) - d - t\] / K and, by default, Fatmin = second zero of the curve = (pi + d - t) / K, Cheneviere's definition (SPEC 19, finding 3). Fatmin can lie beyond the last observed step (extrapolation).

Which rows are fitted

`MFO_kinetics()` fits every row it receives. Cheneviere et al. (2009) fitted exercise steps only, and averaged only steps with RER <= 1.0:

  • `MFO(..., RER_cutoff = 1)` reproduces their step selection;

  • `MFO(..., include_basal = TRUE)` adds the resting row to `MFO_db`, so it is also fitted here. This departs from Cheneviere's procedure in the SIN as well as in the P3.

The SIN is sensitive to the last steps because the curve must reach zero: in the example data (`author = "Frayn"`) the last step (74.7 % VO2max, RER 1.03) has negative fat oxidation.

  • `negative_FAT = "truncate"` (default) sets it to 0 and that point anchors the second zero: d = -0.385, s = 0.910, t = 0.355, FatMax_SIN = 36.2, Fatmin = 76.4 % VO2max.

  • `negative_FAT = "exclude"` or `RER_cutoff = 1` drops it: d = -0.440, s = 0.539, t = 0.023, FatMax_SIN = 33.2, Fatmin = 85.3 % VO2max.

Report which option was used when publishing SIN parameters.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Read dfs
data(list = c("basal_df", "MFO_df", "VO2max_df"), package = "MFO")

# Convert to data.frame
basal_df <- data.frame(basal_df)
MFO_df <- data.frame(MFO_df)
VO2max_df <- data.frame(VO2max_df)

# Calculate MFO and Fatmax
result_MFO <- MFO(step_time = 20,
                 db_MFO = MFO_df,
                 db_basal = basal_df,
                 db_graded = VO2max_df,
                 cv_var = "RER",
                 author = "Frayn")

# Calculate MFO Kinetics
result_kinetics <- MFO_kinetics(result_MFO$MFO_db)

# Fatmin at 5 % of MFO instead of the second zero
MFO_kinetics(result_MFO$MFO_db, fatmin_threshold = 0.05)$Fatmin
} # }
